rubric_definition: After you make the edit that one reviewer is asking for, does the other reviewer's comment still stand? If it is discharged too, the two findings are one defect; if it survives, they are different defects that share a location. If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.
evidence: Finding A objects to a tautological OID assertion inside the "all pg built-in types" loop; Finding B asks to merge a duplicated `queries real tables with rows` test at line 114. Removing the OID assertion leaves the duplicate test intact, and merging the duplicate tests does nothing about the OID assertion.

panel.finding_key: packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts::`expect(columns[0].datatypeid).tobe(expectedoid)` in the all-types loop asserts postgresql's own oids, not any behaviour of the code under test
panel.summary: `expect(columns[0].dataTypeID).toBe(expectedOid)` in the all-types loop asserts PostgreSQL's own OIDs, not any behaviour of the code under test
panel.evidence: Inside the 'check correct cell values for all pg built-in types' loop the first assertion compares the OID reported by pg for `CREATE TABLE (val <type>)` against `types.builtins.<TYPE>` — i.e. pg-types constants against pg's catalog. It cannot fail for any change in datasource.service.ts and is effectively a self-check of the pg library. The adjacent `toCell(rows[0].val)` assertion is the one carrying real signal; the OID line is padding.
